results.claim: For every fixed threshold τ≥2, a simple three-occurrence color sequence encodes a spanning forest with exactly two roots, even root degrees, and odd nonroot degrees.
results.proof_sketch: Let G have N=2n vertices and use q=n−1 colors. For each color c_i, put two stacks of height τ−1 in a first phase, followed by one more such stack per color in a second phase. Require the board to be empty afterward. Since τ−1<τ and 2(τ−1)≥τ, adjacent placement of the first two c_i-stacks would eliminate them and leave the final c_i-stack impossible to eliminate. Thus the first phase leaves N−2 distinct occupied vertices and exactly two empty roots. The final c_i-stack must be placed at an empty common neighbor of its two surviving stacks; adjacency to fewer than both leaves at least one c_i-stack. Direct edges from this center to the two cleared vertices. Every initially occupied vertex is cleared exactly once as a child and hence has exactly one parent, while the roots have none. Following parent pointers strictly decreases clearing time, so it ends at a root and cannot cycle. The N−2 edges therefore form a spanning forest with exactly two rooted components. Children occur in pairs, so roots have even degree and nonroots have one parent plus an even number of children, hence odd degree.

results.claim: For the leaf-corona G of a connected subcubic graph H, the above prefix can empty G if and only if H has a Hamiltonian path.
results.proof_sketch: For |V(H)|=1 the prefix is empty and the equivalence is immediate. Assume |V(H)|≥2, and attach a private leaf v′ to every v∈V(H). From any emptying play obtain the two-root parity forest F. A pendant root has degree zero; every nonroot pendant vertex has its unique edge in F. Both roots cannot be pendant, since they would be two isolated components with vertices left over. If neither is pendant, deleting all pendant edges produces two forest components in H; in each, its root has odd degree and every other vertex even degree, contradicting the handshaking lemma. Hence exactly one root is a pendant a′ and is isolated; the other root r is original. Deleting the leaves gives a spanning tree T of H. If r=a, every degree of T is even, impossible for a nontrivial tree. Otherwise only a and r have odd degree in T. Since H is subcubic, every other vertex has degree two in T; the degree sum forces a and r to have degree one. Thus T is a Hamiltonian path. Conversely, for a Hamiltonian path v_1,…,v_n, take roots v_1′ and v_n. Pair v_n′ with v_{n−1}, then v_{n−1}′ with v_{n−2}, and so on. Each pair is nonadjacent and has the preceding path vertex as an available common neighbor, giving a valid emptying play.

results.claim: Fitting Hexasort is NP-hard for every exact fixed threshold τ≥2, even on graphs of maximum degree four.
results.proof_sketch: Reduce from the standard NP-complete problem Hamiltonian Path on connected graphs of maximum degree three, using the leaf-corona prefix above. Append N fresh colors, each appearing once with height one. These N stacks never merge or vanish when τ≥2, so if k vertices remain occupied after the prefix, precisely N−k suffix stacks can be placed before the board is full. Consequently, all N suffix stacks fit exactly when the board is empty after the prefix. The construction is polynomial, uses only heights τ−1 and 1, and the leaf-corona has maximum degree at most four.

results.claim: Complete classification: the constant-threshold problem is NP-complete for every fixed τ≥2, while τ=1 is trivial.
results.proof_sketch: A certificate lists one chosen vertex per input stack. Each deterministic placement and same-color merge can be simulated with polynomially many integer operations, so Fitting Hexasort is in NP. The reduction proves NP-hardness for every fixed τ≥2; in particular, any promise t≤T with fixed T≥2 remains NP-complete because it contains the exact-t=2 instances. For τ=1, every placed positive-height stack immediately vanishes, so every sequence fits whenever the graph has a vertex; on an empty graph exactly the empty sequence fits.

final_writeup:
The classification is NP-complete for every fixed elimination threshold τ≥2 (indeed already for τ=2 and maximum-degree-four graphs). Threshold one is trivial.

Fix any constant τ≥2. We reduce from Hamiltonian Path on connected graphs H of maximum degree three. Write V(H)={v_1,…,v_n}, with n≥2. Construct G by attaching to every v a new private leaf v′. Thus |V(G)|=N=2n and Δ(G)≤4. Let q=n−1 and introduce colors c_1,…,c_q. Define the prefix

P = (c_1,τ−1),(c_1,τ−1), …, (c_q,τ−1),(c_q,τ−1), (c_1,τ−1),…,(c_q,τ−1).

First consider plays that leave G empty after P. The first two stacks of any c_i cannot be placed adjacently: since τ−1<τ and 2(τ−1)≥τ, they would vanish, after which the last and only remaining c_i-stack could never vanish. Consequently, after the first 2q moves there are exactly 2q=N−2 occupied vertices and two empty vertices.

When the last c_i-stack is played, both earlier c_i-stacks must be removed. Placing it adjacent to zero of them leaves the new stack; placing it adjacent to exactly one eliminates that one but leaves the other. It must therefore be placed at an empty common neighbor of both. The two occupied vertices and the newly placed stack then vanish, leaving the center empty.

Make the two initially empty vertices roots. Whenever the final c_i-stack is placed at x and clears vertices y,z, direct edges xy and xz from parent x to children y,z. Every initially occupied vertex is cleared exactly once as one of these children, so every nonroot has exactly one parent, while the two roots have none. If a parent is not a root, it was cleared strictly earlier than its children. Following parent pointers therefore strictly decreases clearing time and must terminate at a root. Thus the edges form a spanning forest; there are N−2 edges, so it has exactly two components. Children occur in pairs, hence both roots have even forest degree and every nonroot has odd degree.

We now recover a Hamiltonian path in H. In the leaf-corona G, a pendant leaf used as a root must have degree zero, whereas every nonroot pendant leaf has degree one. The two roots cannot both be pendant leaves: both would be isolated, leaving no rooted component for the remaining vertices. If neither root is pendant, all pendant edges belong to the forest. Deleting them yields two forest components in H, each containing one root. In either component its root has odd degree after leaf deletion, while every other vertex has even degree. This contradicts the handshaking lemma, since a graph component cannot have exactly one odd-degree vertex.

Thus precisely one root is a pendant leaf, say a′. It is an isolated component. The other root r is an original vertex, and the remaining forest component contains every other vertex. Delete all pendant vertices. The result T is a spanning tree of H. The edge aa′ is absent, while every other pendant edge is present. If r=a, every vertex of T would have even degree, impossible for a nontrivial tree. Otherwise a and r have odd degree in T and all other vertices have even degree. Because H is subcubic, every vertex other than a,r has degree exactly two in T. The tree degree sum then gives deg_T(a)+deg_T(r)=2, so both are leaves. Hence T is a Hamiltonian path from a to r.

Conversely, suppose H has Hamiltonian path v_1,v_2,…,v_n. Leave v_1′ and v_n initially empty. For i=1,…,n−1, place the first two c_i-stacks on v_{n−i+1}′ and v_{n−i}. These vertices are nonadjacent because v_{n−i+1}′ is private to v_{n−i+1}. For the final c_1-stack use center v_n, clearing v_n′ and v_{n−1}. Next use v_{n−1} for c_2, and continue backward along the path. Each required center was initially empty or was cleared by the preceding move. The final move uses v_2 and clears v_2′ and v_1, leaving G empty.

To obtain Fitting Hexasort, append N stacks (d_1,1),…,(d_N,1), where all d_j are new and distinct. Each permanently occupies one vertex because τ≥2 and its color never recurs. If k vertices are occupied after P, only N−k suffix stacks can be placed. Therefore all N suffix stacks fit if and only if all N vertices were empty after P. This completes the reduction.

Membership in NP follows by recording the chosen vertex for every stack and simulating all moves with polynomially many integer operations. Thus exact fixed-τ Fitting Hexasort is NP-complete for every τ≥2. Equivalently, for every fixed upper bound T≥2, the restriction t≤T is NP-complete because it contains the exact-t=2 subclass. When τ=1, every positive-height stack vanishes immediately, so every sequence fits on a nonempty graph; on an empty graph exactly the empty sequence fits.
